case_name: Rohit Dagar & Ors vs State (Nct Of Delhi) & Anr

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Rohit Dagar & Ors — husband, wife, and others
parties.respondent_defendant: State (NCT of Delhi) & Anr — government and another

facts_of_case: Petitioners seek quashing of FIR No. 433/2019 registered under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC, submitting settlement between parties vide settlement document dated 7.9.2021 and settlement deed dated 14.7.2022.

legal_principles.principle: Criminal cases having overwhelmingly and predominantly civil character, particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes should be quashed when the parties have resolved their entire disputes among themselves.
legal_principles.held: On the other, those criminal cases having overwhelmingly and pre-dominantly civil character, particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes should be quashed when the parties have resolved their entire disputes among themselves.
cited_cases: Narender Singh &Ors. V. State of Punjab; (2014) 6 SCC 466

legal_principles.principle: It is not safe to leave the crime-doer only because he and the victim have settled the dispute amicably or that the victim has been paid compensation.
legal_principles.held: No doubt, crimes are acts which have harmful effect on the public and consist in wrongdoing that seriously endangers and threatens the well-being of the society and it is not safe to leave the crime-doer only because he and the victim have settled the dispute amicably or that the victim has been paid compensation.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Another, (2012) 10 SCC 303
